messages.author: 85710a48a204a0a6
messages.subject: Degrees of Freedom (AMOS-Lavaan)
parts:
Dear Colleagues, 

I'd like the help of someone with expertise in the use of Lavaan.

The issue is that by passing from Amos to Lavaan, I have had a problem with the number of DF reported in the model. 

I have estimated a model with AMOS (with 16 DF) (please see attached)

I have then been asked to check the re-run the model with the satorra-bentler scaled chi-square with robust standard errors. Because Amos does not support this feature, I have run the model in Lavaan with the following code. I have now obtained virtually the same results (in terms of regression weights) but only 13 DF

C.model<-'
MHSc ~ RIDSc 
CM ~ MHSc 
CEVAL ~ MHSc 
PInteraction ~ MHSc 
PInteraction ~ PQuantCont
Pr ~ CM 
Pr ~ CEVAL 
Pr ~ PInteraction
Pr ~ PD 


CEVAL ~~ PInteraction
CEVAL ~~ CM 
PInteraction ~~ CM 
'
fit <- sem(C.model, data = c, estimator = "MLM")
summary(fit, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)
fitMeasures(fit)

I am not an expert in the use of R and even less of the lavaan package. There must be something I am overlooking here. Any suggestion that could point me toward the right direction would be very much appreciated. 

Thank you very much for your time, 

John

Update:

By plotting the model in R, I have realized that it is displaying double arrows between the variables RIDSc, PD, and PQuantCont. I assume these are covariances and might be where the three degrees of freedom are lost in translation. 

I am sure this is a very basic question, and apologies, but there is a way to tell lavaan not to estimate these three paths? It seems to be doing this automatically. 

Really, any suggestion would be much appreciated. 

Thanks again! :)

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Degrees of Freedom (AMOS-Lavaan)
parts:
it's a bit unusual that you don't want to have these paths - it's like a multiple regression, you allow your predictors to correlate, and the multiple regression doesn't make sense if you don't.

But if you really don't want them, fixed.x=FALSE will do it. As in:

fit <- sem(C.model, data = c, estimator = "MLM", fixed.x=FALSE) 

Jeremy

RIDSc ~~ 0* PQuantCont 
PD~~ 0* PQuantCont 
PD~~ 0* RIDSc 

Jeremy

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Degrees of Freedom (AMOS-Lavaan)
parts:
On 05/15/2014 07:12 PM, Jeremy Miles wrote:
>
> Oh, I didn't realize it still put them in by default

The difference between fixed.x=TRUE and fixed.x=FALSE is that the latter
estimates the variances/covariances of the exogenous variables, while
the former simply takes the sample values.

But in both settings, the variances/covariances are always included by
default (if using the sem() or cfa() functions). Forcing the covariances
among exogenous variables to be zero seems strange to me. This may
perhaps make sense in an experimental design, but not for observational
studies.

Yves.
